thread:
monica: FYI -- hit a nasty dup cascade on onboarding sampleapp. repro outline: many clients hit a stale token at once, several do refresh concurrently, each immediately retries, server accepts multiple, downstream sees duplicate webhook deliveries.
raph: annoying. can you paste compact logs? trying to see if its client-side storming.
monica: snippet: `OUT: POST /v1/generate req=aa1` -> `IN: 429 ttl=0` -> SDK instances A,B,C: start refresh (concurrent) -> A refreshed -> A retry succ `gen_01` -> B refreshed -> B retry succ `gen_02` -> C retried -> `gen_03`. webhooks: gen_01/02/03 within ~400ms window.
eli: so this is a classic thundering-retry problem after auth rotation. options: (1) sampleapp should set idempotency-key (recommended), (2) SDK-side leader-lock per-process so only one refresh+retry runs for a given request fingerprint, (3) post-refresh exponential-backoff with jitter to break the herd, (4) short-lived client response-cache of recent request hashes to suppress immediate duplicate sends.
monica: we already teach idempotency in docs, but many onboarding users skip it. Id like pragmatic SDK changes that reduce surprise for new users without surprising streaming behavior.
raph: my vote: default to backoff+jitter on post-refresh retries, add opt-in leader-lock for single-process coordination, and offer an opt-in tiny transient cache (fingerprint -> response-id) for non-streaming calls. leader-lock details: per-request-hash mutex TTL ~500ms so simultaneous refreshes coalesce. Make it off by default (enableRefreshLeaderLock=false).
eli: backoff defaults: baseBackoff=80ms, multiplier=1.8, maxAttempts=3, jitterPct=40% (uniform). Exempt streaming/resume flows. Also emit a diagnostic event `post_auth_retry_cascade` with tags: host_instance, hashed_body, attempt_index so we can detect cascade events.
monica: can we implement a cheap leader-lock without IPC? within a single process z the leader-lock helps only when multiple threads/instances in same process retry. For multi-process/clustered clients you still need backoff. So leader-lock should be opt-in convenience, not a cure-all.
raph: yep. leader-lock name: `enableRefreshLeaderLock`, `refreshLeaderLockTTLms=500`. Transient cache TTL config: `transientRespCacheMs=800` and `transientRespCacheMaxKeys=2048`.
eli: also add env vars for quick testing: RW_SDK_REFRESH_BACKOFF_BASE_MS, RW_SDK_REFRESH_BACKOFF_MULT, RW_SDK_REFRESH_JITTER_PCT. Documented safe defaults should be gentle to avoid visible latency increases.
monica: sampleapp short-term fix: add X-Idempotency-Key derived from user_id + body-hash and consumer dedupe if header present. I'll open a patch.
raph: please also add a short repro harness that fires 50 concurrent clients with coordinated token expiry so SRE can validate before/after metrics.
eli: Ill open SDK issue #7021: "Reduce duplicate accepts from refresh storms: backoff+jitter, optional leader-lock, transient response cache, telemetry" and attach a short benchmark plan.
ci-bot: created issue #7021: "sdk: mitigate post-auth refresh retry storms (backoff, leader-lock, transient-cache, telemetry)"
monica: thanks. follow-ups: (a) update onboarding checklist with explicit idempotency guidance for any externals, (b) sampleapp PR + repro script, (c) SDK PR with configs and telemetry, (d) SRE validation plan.
raph: also call out that server-side dedupe remains recommended for high-safety flows; client mitigations reduce risk but cant guarantee uniqueness across clusters.
eli: agreed. I'll prototype backoff+jitter + diagnostics first and wire up the env flags. leader-lock + cache as opt-in follow-ups.
monica: cool. tagging SRE: @sre-team please volunteer to run the harness when PRs land. thanks :thumbsup:
